How I Can Help

AI can do a lot of the doing now. What I bring is the way I see things, the way I listen, and the way I connect ideas and tell a story.

Pedro sees

Diego hears

I can help you:

I can help you:

Here's a little story about me.

Once upon a time, in a land called Dubai, I was living away from home for the first time.

Before Dubai, I applied to Qatar Airways. I stood in a long queue outside the hotel, in a blazer and a skirt, with more than 900 other candidates. I made it to the final 14, and then I was cut. A few days later, Emirates had an opening. There were about 100 of us that time, and I got in.

Three months in Dubai, I was on the phone with my mom, crying, telling her I wanted to go home. I stayed for four years and five months, and asked “chicken or beef?” more times than I can count.

After flying, I shaped a surfboard on the Gold Coast and tried carpentry back home.

During the lockdown, in the final leg of my MBA, I started Feelings Coffee, a box I wished existed. This time, the case study was live: real customers, me in every role, and the occasional curveball. After that, I went back to teaching Tagalog, this time on YouTube, as a one-woman show.

I taught myself data storytelling before AI could do it for me, and I learned how to build websites.

Today, I'm the Lead Storyteller at Good Cup.

Those three octopuses started as keychains I designed for 3D printing. The rest of the story is in the chapters below.

If Life Had Chapters

Some chapters are about my work, some are about me ♡.

  1. 1Chicken or Beef?More than four years as a flight attendant with Emirates Airlines.Emirates

    It's impossible to fit my adventures in one paragraph. But if we had met on one of the flights, our conversation would have probably started with, “Chicken or beef?”

    Back then, planes were like a hop-on, hop-off bus. I rarely flew with the same person twice. And my colleagues and passengers were from different parts of the world.

    • Cross-cultural communication
    • Service
    • Reading people
  2. 2Sawdust ♡After flying, I wanted to try things I had never done.Gold Coast

    I enrolled myself in a surfboard shaping workshop on the Gold Coast and a carpentry workshop in Manila.

    I once wanted to be a furniture designer and a carpenter.

    • CookingLearned the way most people do: by trying, tasting and trying again.
    • 3D printingDesigning printable keychains. See chapter 8.
  3. 3A Box of FeelingsA coffee box I wished existed.Feelings Coffee

    It started during the lockdown. The original idea was closer to Leafly than to the sampler box it turned into.

    I was talking to one of my Tagalog students at the time, who was well-versed in startups. It was through him that I learned of Y Combinator. He was the first person who believed in the idea. “Your idea has bones,” he said.

    This was during the final leg of my MBA, when the last exam was cancelled because of the pandemic. In school, problems came as case studies: something that had already happened to some big company, discussed in one subject. The risk stayed inside the controlled environment of a university: you pass or you fail.

    Feelings Coffee, my first venture, was a tiny (microscopic, really) attempt at business. It was happening live, and I was the one making the calls: marketing, packaging, operations, finance, logistics, sourcing and every problem in between. Unlike the case studies, the consequences were unknown. The future wasn’t set yet, and my decisions were about to shape it.

    At first, it was all me. Eventually, I brought in an illustrator, architect and artist, who happened to be my sister. Through this, I learned how to delegate and communicate. Skills that are key to running a business.

    Feelings Coffee was an exercise in grit and perseverance.

    The boxes still live on Instagram.

    • Brand building
    • Product experience design
    • Copywriting
    • Visual direction
    • Customer experience

  5. 5712 Flights, 92 Airports, 60 Cities, 35 CountriesI taught myself data storytelling and data visualization.Data viz

    One of the first stories I told with data was my own: how much did I travel as cabin crew?

    4.3years
    712flights
    92airports
    60cities
    35countries
    5continents

    AI can draw a chart in seconds now. But data only lands when people can understand it, so how you present it matters as much as the data itself.

    I made the dashboards below in Tableau, before AI could build them. I cleaned the data, looked for the patterns and decided what to show.

  8. 8The Key of Ibong AdarnaIf you have the key, you can unlock many doors.Keychain studio

    Keychain Studio has a few keys. It also has three octopus keychains for 3D printing: see no evil, hear no evil and speak no evil.

    I'm fascinated by octopuses. They have three hearts, blue blood and nine brains. They're so different, and that resonates with me. I've never really felt like I belonged anywhere, not even in my own family. That's not meant to sound dramatic. It's just the feeling of being different.

    It started with a visual idea: the octopuses turning gray. That reminded me of the Ibong Adarna, whose songs put you to sleep before it turns you to stone. There's a story behind the keychains, but I'm still in the process of writing it.

    I built a little studio to preview the colors and finishes before printing. I made it by experimenting with AI. Drag to spin them.

    see no evil · hear no evil · speak no evil

  9. 9Dear Mom ♡This is a letter to my mom.A letter

    To my anchor.

    I'd like to think my mom was the first person who loved me and the first person I loved, my first connection to this world, literally and figuratively. I know I've changed over the years, and I'll keep changing. But some things are worth keeping the same, and I don't want to lose sight of that.

    Dear Mom,

    When I was crying on the phone in Dubai, you were the one I called.

    The truth is, I don't know what to write to you yet. I just know it starts with thank you.

The end, for now
